image_description: Two male ducks (drakes) swimming in rippled water. The duck on the left appears to be a Mallard with an iridescent green head, white neck ring, and grey body. The duck on the right has a black head, white breast, and grey flanks, resembling a Northern Pintail or similar species. Both are floating low in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both ducks display characteristic broad, flat bills. The left duck's bill is yellowish-green, and the right duck's bill is dark grey/black, matching the description.
Visible eyes on both subjects are small and dark, consistent with duck anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both bodies sit low in the water, appearing streamlined and buoyant. Plumage texture appears dense and smooth, repelling water effectively.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left duck clearly exhibits the Mallard pattern (green head, white ring, grey body). The right duck shows distinct breeding coloration (black head, white breast), fitting the general criteria for drake plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ducks are swimming, and their legs/feet are submerged and completely occluded by the water and body angle. Cannot verify webbing or leg position.
Wings are folded against the body but visible. They appear broad and taper to a point at the tail, consistent with resting duck anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail of the right duck is visible and short. While the specific 'curl' is subtle due to the angle, the short, pointed tail structure is present.

The transition from the grey flank to the tail feathers on the right duck is slightly indistinct, with a minor blending of textures that lacks the crisp definition of individual feathers seen in high-quality photography.
